source.what: Joby Aviation footer on the careers page — the footerWrapper (blue link field) plus the footerCreative band (layered horizon graphic) beneath it. Distilled for structure, layout, typography and motion.
source.method: Chromium (ms-playwright chromium-1234) driven by puppeteer-core, one isolated browser context per width. Three viewports: 1440x900, 834x1112, 390x844, deviceScaleFactor 1, page scrolled to the document end and settled 2s so the footer reveal completed. Page-transition and cookie overlays were removed from the DOM before measurement — the site's page-transition layer is what blanked the footer in the naive full-page capture. Values from getComputedStyle, getBoundingClientRect, resolved :root custom properties, the authored Footer-module CSS rules read out of the document stylesheets, and inline SVG geometry (viewBox, rect x/y/width/height, fill) read from the DOM. Collision tests compare real client rects, not assumptions.
gaps: The footer reveal is driven by --footer-up, measured as 0vh at the page top and 40vh once the footer is in view (a 360px translateY at a 900px viewport). The interpolation curve and the scroll trigger point were not isolated; only the two endpoint values are measured.

The newsletter's filled state (input:not(:placeholder-shown), which widens the field to 41.7rem and lifts the title and disclaimer by 8.6rem) was read from authored CSS but not exercised, because typing an address was out of scope for a layout capture.
The newsletter success and error states were not exercised; only their authored rules were read.

The mobile variant's second SVG (footerCreativeSVGMobile) resolves to display:none at all three widths measured, so the intended mobile graphic was not observed rendering. What renders at 390 is the desktop SVG scaled by its viewBox.

The footer creative artwork's own internals are only partly resolved: it is a single inline SVG with 7 rects, 1 path and 1 group, and the artwork appears to be one wing/horizon curve. The individual path geometry beyond the captured bounding boxes was not traced.
Hover and focus states on footer links (a 1.5px underline scaling in from the left, 1px on sub-links) were read from authored CSS, not captured as states.
Only the careers page footer was captured. The footer is a site-wide component, so cross-template consistency is assumed rather than verified.
source.notes: The user described the structure as footerWrapper with footerCreative underneath. Measured, that is half right and the difference matters. footerWrapper is a blue (#007AE5) container with overflow hidden that holds the <footer> grid; footerCreative sits OUTSIDE the wrapper, as a sibling further down the page in a separate SectionWrapper, carrying the dark blue #1C3F99 background and the horizon SVG. So the two are adjacent page sections, not parent and child. The wrapper is 900px tall at 1440 and the footer grid fills it exactly, with the creative band 448.2px below. Two real defects were found and are recorded as negative evidence: the footer grid reserves a 700px hole between its left and right column groups, and at 390px the logo and the newsletter both collide with the Explore link list.

parts.name: Blue field, then horizon band
parts.description: The footer is two stacked page sections, not one. A blue field carries all the links, the logo and the newsletter; beneath it a separate dark-blue band carries a layered horizon graphic whose coloured strata continue the page's palette. The band has no text at all — it is pure surface, 448.2px of it at 1440, closing the page on an image rather than on information.
parts.entry_test: End the footer at the link field and the page stops on a flat colour; the layering of the horizon band is what gives the page a floor. The band is identity-carrying and would fail the removal test.
parts.recipe: Build two sibling sections. Section one: a wrapper with background var(--color-blue) and overflow hidden, containing the footer grid. Section two: a band with background var(--color-dark-blue), position relative, width 100%, pointer-events none, holding the SVG absolutely at bottom 0 left 0 width 100%, z-index 2. Note the wrapper does NOT contain the band — they are adjacent siblings in the page flow. Heights: wrapper 900px at 1440 (matching the viewport), 1112px at 834, 844px at 390; band 448.2px at 1440, 259.6px at 834, 590.7px at 390.

checks.check: The link field and the horizon band are separate stacked sections, not one container
The horizon band carries no text content at all
The band sits below the link field with no gap between them
The band's background is the darker blue and the field's is the brighter blue
The band is non-interactive (pointer-events none)

evidence: measured at 1440: footerWrapper box y 10064.8, h 900, bg rgb(0,122,229); footerCreative box y 10964.8, h 448.2, bg rgb(28,63,153) — the band begins exactly where the wrapper ends (10064.8 + 900 = 10964.8)
authored: .footerWrapper { position:relative; height:fit-content; background-color:var(--color-blue); overflow:hidden }
authored: .footerCreative { position:relative; width:100%; background-color:var(--color-dark-blue); pointer-events:none }
footerCreative innerText is empty at all three widths

parts.name: Layered horizon
parts.description: The closing graphic is four horizontal colour strata meeting a single large curve that sweeps up from the bottom left to the top right, so the bands appear to be cut by a wing or a horizon line. The strata step from dark blue through pale blue and bright blue back to dark blue, and their heights decrease sharply toward the bottom (296, 296, 182, 57 units in a 737-unit box). The curve is drawn as one path on a group that overhangs its container by 8 units on the left and 170 above the top, so the artwork bleeds past its own bounds.
parts.entry_test: Flatten the strata into a single fill and the footer loses its only graphic; it is the one drawn gesture on the whole page and the reason the page ends rather than stops.
parts.recipe: One inline SVG, viewBox 0 0 1600 737, no explicit width/height, positioned absolute bottom 0 left 0 width 100% z-index 2. Inside: a group offset x=8 y=-170, containing four full-width rects at y 202/498/680 with height 296/182/57 plus the group's top rect. Fills in stacking order: dark blue #1C3F99, pale blue #C1DFEF, bright blue #007AE5, dark blue #1C3F99. The cutting curve is a single path, d='M1600 737C1600 737 1283.98 736.995 600 737C1600 736.989 1600 -0.000151364 1600 -0.000151364L1600 737Z', fill #646464 in the captured state — the visible colours come from the rects, so treat the path as the mask/cut shape rather than a fill. Do not change the viewBox aspect on mobile; it scales by width only.

checks.check: The graphic is four stacked colour strata cut by one large curve
Strata heights decrease toward the bottom of the band
The artwork bleeds past its container on at least one axis
The SVG is positioned to the band's bottom edge, not its top
The graphic carries no text or logo

parts.name: Four link rails on the same tracks
parts.description: The four link lists are placed on fixed spans of the shared 16-track grid — columns 1-2, 11-2, 13-2, 15-2 — so each list is exactly two tracks wide (156px at 1440) regardless of how long its longest link is. The rails are constant and the text fits inside them.
parts.entry_test: Size each list to its own content and the right-hand cluster loses its shared left edges; the fixed rail width is what makes four unequal lists read as a set of columns.
parts.recipe: grid-column 1 / span 2 for the sub-links, 11 / span 2 for main, 13 / span 2 for explore, 15 / span 2 for social; grid-row 1 for the three right-hand lists, auto for the sub-links. Each list is display flex, column-direction, width fit-content, and resolves to exactly two tracks: 156px at 1440, 156px at 1200, 156px at 1024, 156px at 834. Critically: do not adopt this page's interior hole. Reserving rails at column 1 and at columns 11-16 leaves columns 3 through 10 (x 250 to 860, about 610px at 1440) empty on the same row. A rail system must either declare that gap as an intentional spacer span or redistribute the rails; the page leaves it undeclared, which is the defect.

checks.check: Each list is placed by column span, not by content width
All four lists resolve to the same width (two tracks)
Interior columns between the left and right clusters are accounted for as a declared span
The three right-hand lists share a grid row
A list's longest link still fits inside its two-track rail

parts.name: Label row, then the links
parts.description: Each list opens with a small label in the 12px caption size, then a 32px gap, then the links themselves at 18px. The label is not a heading — it is the same 12px caption style used elsewhere on the site — and it is separated from its list by a fixed margin rather than by a type-size jump.
parts.entry_test: Set the label and the links at one size and the columns lose their headers; the caption-size label plus the fixed 32px break is what makes a list read as a labelled group rather than a run of links.
parts.recipe: First li in each list carries margin-bottom 3.2rem and its anchor is set at the 12px/450 caption style; subsequent links are 18px/450. The gap between the label li and the second li measures exactly 32px on all three right-hand lists. The sub-links list (legal links and copyright) has no label and no such gap — every item is 12px with 0 gap, so it reads as a footnote block rather than a titled column. That difference is deliberate and should be preserved: three labelled columns plus one unlabelled footnote list.

parts.name: Row two carries logo and newsletter
parts.description: The second grid row pairs the logo on the far left with the newsletter block on the right, sharing the row but not the alignment: the logo is explicitly aligned to the row's end while the newsletter sits at its own natural top, so the two halves of the row are deliberately not on a shared baseline.
parts.entry_test: Align the logo to the row's top and it floats away from the foot of the column beside it; the end-alignment is what anchors the mark to the bottom of the link block above.
parts.recipe: Row 2 holds logoContainer at grid-column 1 / span 4 with align-self end, and the newsletter at 11 / span 5. At 1440 those resolve to logo x 40 w 176 h 52 and newsletter x 900 w 414 h 70.2. Because the two are on the same row but different alignments, their tops differ: logo y 10823.8 against newsletter y 10805.6, an 18.2px offset. That offset is the row's design, not a bug — but it must be an intentional consequence of align-self, never of an accidental margin. Do not copy the row spacing: the two rows sit 525.8px apart because the row is implicit inside a fixed 900px field and absorbs all remaining height as one void.

parts.name: Underline field that grows on entry
parts.description: The signup is a bare underlined input with no box, set at display size so it reads as a line of type rather than a form control, with a small arrow to its right. On typing, the field widens and the title and disclaimer slide up out of the way, so the control changes shape and its surroundings reflow together.
parts.entry_test: Box the input and the footer gains a form where it had a line of text; the underline treatment and the widening are what keep the signup in the footer's typographic register.
parts.recipe: Input: width 16ch, background none, colour var(--color-white), border-radius 0, font-size 2.8rem weight 500 line-height 120% letter-spacing -0.056rem, with a bottom border only. On :not(:placeholder-shown) the width becomes 41.7rem. The submit is an absolutely positioned 1.8rem arrow at right, translated -50% on Y, pointer-events none until the field has content, at which point it takes the light colour and becomes interactive. The title and disclaimer lift 8.6rem on the same trigger. Title also takes the dimmed blue at that point. Durations: width and border-bottom .4s in-out-cubic; transform .4s out-cubic; title colour .4s in-out-cubic.

checks.check: The input is underline-only with no box, border or fill

parts.name: Footer-up reveal variable
parts.description: The footer's content is offset downward and rises into place as the footer scrolls into view, driven by a single custom property rather than by per-element animation. Every list shares the property, so the whole set lifts as one surface.
parts.entry_test: Animate the lists individually and they arrive out of step; the single shared offset is what makes the footer read as one panel sliding up rather than four lists appearing.
parts.recipe: Declare --footer-up on the footer and transform each list by translateY(var(--footer-up)). Measured: 0vh while the footer is off screen (transform none), 40vh once the footer is in view — 360px at a 900px viewport. Drive the property from a scroll-position value so every list moves by the same amount at the same time. Do not attach separate entrance animations to the four lists, and do not animate the logo or newsletter on this property — only the link lists carry it.

parts.name: Dark strip at the foot of the grid
parts.description: The grid's bottom edge carries a dark-blue strip drawn as a pseudo-element, 3.4rem tall, so the link field ends on a band of the darker colour rather than on bare blue — the strip pre-echoes the horizon band below it and ties the two sections together.
parts.entry_test: Remove the strip and the blue field meets the horizon band as a hard colour change; the strip is what makes the transition read as a deliberate step.
parts.recipe: footer::after, position absolute, bottom 0, left 0, width 100%, height 3.4rem, background var(--color-dark-blue). Rendered height 34px at a 10px root. Use the same dark-blue token as the horizon band so the strip and the band are literally the same colour.

parts.name: Narrow-width collision avoidance
parts.description: This is a negative move: the requirement the page fails. When the footer stacks at narrow widths the logo, the newsletter and the link lists must occupy separate vertical space. On this page they do not — at 390px the logo and the newsletter both overlap the Explore link list, because the stacked grid rows and the absolutely positioned newsletter disclaimer share the same band of vertical space.
parts.entry_test: Not a gesture to copy — the opposite. Recorded because a footer rubric that omits it will happily reproduce the fault. Overlapping footer content fails the removal test in reverse: it must be removed.
parts.recipe: At narrow widths give every footer block its own row and verify with real client rects that no two blocks intersect. Do not rely on grid row order alone when a block is absolutely positioned inside another (the newsletter's disclaimer is position absolute, so the newsletter's own box does not grow to contain it). Measured collisions at 390: logo box x 16.6 y 183.5 w 59.5 h 36.6 against explore list x 16.6 y 130.8 w 356.8 h 93.2 — overlapping; newsletter box x 135.5 y 172.1 w 237.8 h 48 against the same explore list — overlapping. The sub-links list at 390 is also fully off-screen above the field (y -228) because the lists keep their shared offset while the field is shorter than their total height.

checks.check: At the narrowest width no two footer blocks' client rects intersect
Blocks that stack are given separate grid rows rather than overlapping implicitly
An absolutely positioned child (the disclaimer) does not escape its parent's reserved space
No footer content sits outside the field's visible bounds at any width
The shared reveal offset does not push content past the field's top

limitations: The reveal curve is not characterised. --footer-up measures 0vh at the page top and 40vh at the document end (360px at a 900px viewport), but the interpolation between those endpoints and the scroll position that triggers the transition were not isolated.

The newsletter's filled state was not exercised: the field widening to 41.7rem and the 8.6rem lift of the title and disclaimer are read from authored CSS, not measured in a live state. Typing an address was out of scope for a layout capture.
The newsletter success and error states were not exercised; only their authored rules were read.

A second SVG exists in the markup (footerCreativeSVGMobile) but resolves to display:none at all three widths measured, so the intended mobile artwork was never observed. What renders at 390 is the desktop artwork scaled to width, which is why the horizon curve is proportionally much larger on mobile.

The footer field's height tracks the viewport exactly at all three widths measured (900/1112/844). Whether that is authored behaviour or a coincidence of content plus stretched rows was not resolved; the authored rule is height fit-content, so the match is likely emergent and may break at other viewport heights.

Two layout defects are recorded as negative evidence and are NOT targets: the undeclared 610px interior gap between the left and right column clusters on row 1, and the mobile collisions where the logo and newsletter overlap the Explore list at 390px. An applier must not reproduce either.

The sub-links list renders entirely above the field's top edge at 390px (y -228) because the four lists keep their shared offset while the stacked field is shorter than their combined height. This is a third defect, recorded in the same negative-evidence move.
Hover and focus states (the 1.5px and 1px underlines) were read from authored CSS, not captured.

The horizon graphic is described from its geometry — 7 rects, 1 path, 1 group on a 1600x737 viewBox — and from a rendered screenshot; the individual path curves beyond the captured bounding boxes were not traced, so the exact silhouette is characterised rather than specified.
Only the careers page footer was captured; cross-template consistency is assumed, not verified.
